extracted.THIS_FIXTURE_RESOLVES_THE_APPARENT_PRICE: The brief presented the Nov-2025 figures (~$350 Ozempic/Wegovy, ~$346 Zepbound) and the live-site figures (~$199, ~$299) as CONFLICTING. Index-mediated White House text indicates they are NOT contradictory: $350/$346 are stated as AVERAGE prices and $199/$299 as 'as low as' LOWEST-DOSE prices, in the SAME sentence structure. They are two different statistics describing one program, not two competing readings. No averaging or reconciliation was performed by me - the source itself states both.

zepbound.list_price_discrepancy: This text gives Zepbound list as $1,088. The brief cited $1,087 and $1,059-$1,086. Aggregators cite $1,086.37. FOUR different values for one list price; none directly read from Lilly. Unresolved.

extracted.launch_manufacturers: AstraZeneca, Eli Lilly, EMD Serono, Novo Nordisk, Pfizer - the first five to reach MFN pricing deals
extracted.drug_count_at_launch: Over 40 drugs at launch (CBS News secondary reporting says 43), with plans to add more
extracted.claimed_annual_saving: GLP-1 users without insurance coverage expected to save $3,000 per year via TrumpRx.gov
extracted.mechanism: Patients search for a drug and see savings available via a manufacturer coupon or by purchasing directly from the manufacturer. TrumpRx is a REFERRAL/COMPARISON storefront, not itself a pharmacy or seller.
extracted.later_expansion: A further fact sheet dated May 2026 announces an 'Expansion of TrumpRx.gov to Bring Americans Transparency and Choice on Everyday Medicines', and a CEA analysis PDF 'Savings from Most-Favored-Nation Drug Pricing Policy' is dated May 2026. Prices may have moved AGAIN between the Feb 5 launch and today (2026-07-30); the brief's 'more recent readings' are not necessarily current.
